links.comparator_used: Zero-shot direct-answer prompting on the same model
links.outcome: Chance-corrected recognition of emotion from body language (EU-Emotion Stimulus Set)
links.effect: CoT improved Gemini Pro 2.0 (OR = 3.97, p < .001) and mitigated its positivity bias. It impaired Gemini Flash 2.0 (OR = 0.40, p < .001).
links.tradeoff: In the smaller Gemini Flash 2.0, CoT created a specific blind spot for negative emotions, which may compromise clinical safety.
links.quote: We conclude that CoT is not a universal facilitator for emotion recognition; rather, its effectiveness is contingent on model capacity, and its misapplication to smaller models may compromise clinical safety.

links.outcome: Chance-corrected recognition (CCR) of emotion from body language
links.effect: FlashThinking CCR = 0.463, 95% CI [0.310, 0.621]. Gemini Pro 2.0, a generalist, reached CCR = 0.722, 95% CI [0.590, 0.838], and was on par with the human benchmark (0.717).
links.quote: The specialized reasoning model (FlashThinking) achieved a Chance-Corrected Recognition (CCR) score of 0.463, 95% CI [0.310, 0.621], failing to outperform generalist architectures.
